marta: FYI customer BlueHarbor reporting a sudden uptick in 429s around 09:12 UTC. Looks sustained for ~15m, mostly on /v1/chat/stream. They say nothing changed on their side. sample headers pasted below. Anyone see obvious platform-side throttle or is this classic client concurrency+minute-boundary?

eli: Can you paste tenant id + plan and a quick histogram? streaming usually triggers different throttles. Also which region?

marta: tenant=blueharbor-prod, plan=growth, region=us-west-2. From logs: 80% of 429s are for streaming POSTs that start near top-of-minute. Header dump: ```
POST /v1/chat/stream 200/429
x-rw-rpm-limit: 1200
x-rw-rpm-remaining: 0
x-rw-tpm-limit: 20000
x-rw-tpm-remaining: 18400
x-request-id: req_9a3b
```

marta: pattern looks like a bunch of short-lived streaming connections that open at the same second every minute (cron-ish). Could be many lambda instances or a scheduled job.

sachin: that x-rw-rpm-remaining=0 confirms RPM cap hit. Streaming endpoints count as requests per connection open, so concurrent streams that reconnect each minute will spike RPM. Two quick ways: (1) advise client to reuse long-lived streams / multiplex, (2) stagger their cron to spread across minute. We can also temporarily bump their RPM if urgent.

jess: I can open a support escalation for a short-term quota bump. Do we need logs for a formal bump?

eli: yes please attach request samples (x-request-id list) + a short replay of the spike window. Also check whether they use HTTP/2 multiplexing — many clients open N parallel HTTP/1 connections which counts heavier.

marta: repro curl to simulate (single-threaded):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 120); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' &
done
wait
```

marta: I ran a small run and hit 429s after ~85 requests.

eli: mitigation options for the SDK: increase backoff base and jitter, add session pooling so you don't open a new connection per request, and for streaming prefer a single persistent connection per worker. Typical advice: 500ms -> 1500-3000ms randomized retry for 429s during minute peaks.

sachin: operational note: our edge uses a leaky-bucket with a 60s refill. If many connections align at t=00 of the minute, you can exhaust tokens instantly even if average rates are OK. We should add a short doc blurb for customers explaining "minute-boundary confluence" and how to detect it via x-rw-rpm-remaining header patterns.

jess: Created escalation INC-12345 for a 24h RPM bump and asked BlueHarbor to stagger their cron by 15s increments and try session reuse. I included sample curl and SDK suggestions.

infra-bot: quota change request created: INC-12345 — assigned to eng-ops. :eyes:

marta: thanks — I'll send a quick how-to note to the customer with repro, request-ids, and the SDK backoff patch to try now. If we still see 429s after staggering, we'll move to a temporary reserved capacity offer. :thumbsup:
